pr.body:
## Summary This pull request introduces a new feature to manage calendar cache data, including the ability to view cache status and delete cached data. It also includes several supporting updates to repositories, APIs, and UI components. Below is a summary of the most important changes grouped by theme. ### New Feature: Calendar Cache Management * Added a `deleteCache` mutation to the TRPC `calendarsRouter`, enabling users to delete cached calendar data by credential ID. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsxR27-R33](diffhunk://#diff-9e053175cc6dfb5717313e0587a730fff132f9d3c1200204f0ce8dac53a19280R27-R33)`) * Introduced the `deleteCacheHandler` to handle cache deletion logic, including validation of user access to the specified credential. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.tsR1-R33](diffhunk://#diff-572888b8e0555167a5787847f29d5a46623eff170491acc0654e916f5b4afd18R1-R33)`) * Updated the `connectedCalendarsHandler` to enrich calendar data with cache status (`cacheUpdatedAt`) by querying the `CalendarCacheRepository`. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.tsR27-R39](diffhunk://#diff-3f6a556ad60f26d0162770fcd81b5bddeb6ab0437552ac792045c3cd2608d710R27-R39)`) ### UI Enhancements * Created a new `CredentialActionsDropdown` component to display cache status and provide options to delete cached data or disconnect integrations. (`[packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsxR1-R134](diffhunk://#diff-c78273434b95ab8276bb5eb24d9bc088b10af029388bdcd08cbe478f44269b31R1-R134)`) * Replaced the `DisconnectIntegration` component with `CredentialActionsDropdown` in the `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` UI, integrating the new cache management functionality. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L5-R5)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L70-L81)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L125-L135)`) ### Repository and Database Updates * Added a `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method to the `CalendarCacheRepository` and its mock implementation to fetch cache statuses for multiple credentials. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b36c72c0db751ba0cafe234dfa150817672869825333c22b074c4977a6135b8dR30-R32)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ceffbae9ef3da413495feac73a341672e77ffaf493cf67ada0b637ead80ded38R26-R30)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4cf8d3089fad7b6c8fe4172d8d42147f136b65baf30b726e57b9b10d179d4a99R172-R188)`) * Introduced a new `updateManyByCredentialId` method in the `SelectedCalendarRepository` to update multiple calendars by credential ID. (`[packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.tsR400-R406](diffhunk://#diff-ccb4eecfa701e5b0c7d6ba87dcc550cdf3700a63ee252849045611599ecb9273R400-R406)`) * Added an `updatedAt` column to the `CalendarCache` table in the database schema and Prisma model to track the last update timestamp. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9f597bd98bbcfdcf4861ee7bf0c238e7dfe54b456ceb69b852aaf3979c4102cfR1-R8)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-56fa4d384ba6fb94b130e9eb42c5cad00734b025ebd6c197f76873469725ae87R1718)`) ### Localization and Strings * Added new localization strings for cache management actions, such as "Cache Status," "Delete cached data," and "Cache deleted successfully." (`[apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.jsonR3376-R3382](diffhunk://#diff-57de4b8e5231f1d699891d98b0381d56e9e24537b0ca5420d1fba4f0597370bcR3376-R3382)`) ### Miscellaneous * Updated `package.json` to replace `ts-node` with `npx tsx` for running the `dev:cron` script. (`[apps/web/package.jsonL11-R11](diffhunk://#diff-14b60f636e1a2b0061da57aaf231cb1ed15a5dc0c592425ed82e58fec95d42d8L11-R11)`) ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human **🔴 High Priority (5 items)** - [x] **Verify deleteCache tRPC mutation exists** - The component references `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache.useMutation()` but this mutation implementation is not visible in the PR changes. Check if this endpoint exists or needs to be created. - [x] **End-to-end testing with Google Calendar** - Install a Google Calendar integration and verify the credential-level dropdown appears, shows cache status, and deletion flow works correctly with confirmation dialog. - [x] **Test cache status display logic** - Verify that `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamps are correctly formatted and displayed only for Google Calendar credentials with actual cache data. - [x] **Confirm repository pattern correctness** - Test that `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` returns accurate data and the credential-to-cache mapping works properly in the UI. - [x] **Verify dropdown conditional rendering** - Ensure the dropdown only appears for Google Calendar credentials and handles edge cases (no cache, disabled integrations, etc.). **Recommended Test Plan:** 1. Connect a Google Calendar integration to trigger cache creation 2. Navigate to `/apps/installed/calendar` 3. Verify dropdown appears on Google Calendar credential with cache status and timestamp 4. Test "Delete cached data" action shows confirmation dialog 5. Confirm cache deletion works and UI updates appropriately 6. Test "Remove App" functionality still works correctly --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD UI["CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx
(New Component)"]:::major-edit Handler["connectedCalendars.handler.ts
(Updated tRPC Handler)"]:::major-edit RepoInterface["calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts
(Updated Interface)"]:::minor-edit RepoImpl["calendar-cache.repository.ts
(Updated Implementation)"]:::minor-edit RepoMock["calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts
(Updated Mock)"]:::minor-edit Translations["common.json
(Added Translation Keys)"]:::minor-edit UI -->|"Uses repository via tRPC"| Handler Handler -->|"Calls getCacheStatusByCredentialIds"| RepoImpl RepoImpl -->|"Implements"| RepoInterface RepoMock -->|"Implements"| RepoInterface UI -->|"Uses translation keys"| Translations subgraph Legend L1[Major Edit]:::major-edit L2[Minor Edit]:::minor-edit L3[Context/No Edit]:::context end classDef major-edit fill:#90EE90 classDef minor-edit fill:#87CEEB classDef context fill:#FFFFFF ``` ### Notes - **Session Details**: Requested by @zomars, implemented in Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/24545e0980df465995521419432a2a52 - **SelectedCalendar.updatedAt Usage**: Currently only updated in backend via Google webhook handler but not displayed in frontend. Frontend uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache. Consider if SelectedCalendar.updatedAt update should be removed. - **Import Path Resolution**: Had to fix UI component import paths during development - watch for potential module resolution issues in different environments. - **Testing Limitation**: Local testing was limited due to no installed calendar integrations - end-to-end verification with real Google Calendar data is essential.

raw_findings.body: The handler always executes a real prisma.calendarCache.groupBy query and surfaces cacheUpdatedAt in the UI even when the calendar-cache feature is globally disabled, contradicting the established gating pattern (CalendarCache.init returns the mock when disabled) and adding an unconditional DB query per request.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cache status UI and DB queries occur even when calendar caching is disabled, showing stale/irrelevant cache data and diverging from the mock/flag contract.
raw_findings.impact: The handler always executes a real prisma.calendarCache.groupBy query and surfaces cacheUpdatedAt in the UI even when the calendar-cache feature is globally disabled, contradicting the established gating pattern (CalendarCache.init returns the mock when disabled) and adding an unconditional DB query per request.
raw_findings.root_cause: Direct construction of CalendarCacheRepository instead of using the feature-flag-aware CalendarCache.init factory that the codebase uses everywhere else.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Obtain the repository via CalendarCache.init(null) (or an equivalent flag-aware factory) so the mock is used and no cache status is shown when the feature is disabled.
raw_findings.title: connectedCalendars handler bypasses calendar-cache feature flag by instantiating CalendarCacheRepository directly
raw_findings.trigger: Any user loads connected calendars while the global "calendar-cache" feature flag is disabled (the case CalendarCacheRepositoryMock exists for).

raw_findings.body: tRPC surfaces the plain Error as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) instead of a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code, so clients cannot distinguish an authorization failure from a server fault and monitoring records spurious 500s.
raw_findings.evidence: throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied");
raw_findings.failure_mode: Authorization failures are misreported as internal server errors to clients and observability tooling.
raw_findings.impact: tRPC surfaces the plain Error as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) instead of a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code, so clients cannot distinguish an authorization failure from a server fault and monitoring records spurious 500s.
raw_findings.root_cause: New handler uses a generic Error where the tRPC layer expects TRPCError codes to communicate client-side failure semantics.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" }) (or "FORBIDDEN") as other viewer handlers do for missing/unowned resources.
raw_findings.title: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError for authorization failure
raw_findings.trigger: A user calls viewer.calendars.deleteCache with a credentialId they do not own (or a nonexistent/team-owned credential where userId is null).

raw_findings.body: The cache_last_updated timestamp is always rendered in US date/time format (MM/DD/YY, 12-hour clock) regardless of the user's locale, producing inconsistent and potentially confusing localized UI.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Non-English users see US-formatted timestamps embedded in otherwise translated text.
raw_findings.impact: The cache_last_updated timestamp is always rendered in US date/time format (MM/DD/YY, 12-hour clock) regardless of the user's locale, producing inconsistent and potentially confusing localized UI.
raw_findings.root_cause: Locale string hardcoded in the new Intl.DateTimeFormat call while the surrounding component is fully localized.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the user's locale (e.g., from useLocale's i18n.language) to Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of hardcoding "en-US".
raw_findings.title: Cache timestamp is hardcoded to en-US locale ignoring the user's locale
raw_findings.trigger: A user with a non-English locale (the component already calls useLocale for translations) opens the credential dropdown showing cache status.

raw_findings.body: The UI shows an active 'Cache Status / Last updated' entry and a delete option for cache data that is already expired and unusable, misrepresenting cache freshness to the user.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale/expired cache rows are presented as live cache status in the settings UI.
raw_findings.impact: The UI shows an active 'Cache Status / Last updated' entry and a delete option for cache data that is already expired and unusable, misrepresenting cache freshness to the user.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new groupBy query omits the expiresAt filter that every other read path in this repository applies.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } to the where clause (matching getCachedAvailability's filter) or expose expiry so the UI can distinguish expired caches.
raw_findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds reports status for expired cache rows
raw_findings.trigger: A credential has only CalendarCache rows whose expiresAt is in the past (cache no longer served by getCachedAvailability, which filters expiresAt >= now).

raw_findings.body: SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is bumped for every calendar under the credential — including calendars whose cache was not refreshed in this call — and the update only works because Prisma implicitly injects @updatedAt into an empty data object, an obscure side effect that is easy to break during refactoring.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Freshness timestamps are set on rows that were not refreshed, and the intended timestamp bump silently disappears if the implicit @updatedAt behavior changes.
raw_findings.impact: SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is bumped for every calendar under the credential — including calendars whose cache was not refreshed in this call — and the update only works because Prisma implicitly injects @updatedAt into an empty data object, an obscure side effect that is easy to break during refactoring.
raw_findings.root_cause: New updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty update object and a credential-wide predicate instead of an explicit field update scoped to the refreshed calendars.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass an explicit { updatedAt: new Date() } payload and scope the update to the selectedCalendars actually refreshed (e.g., by externalId/eventTypeId) rather than all rows for the credential.
raw_findings.title: Empty-data updateMany relies on implicit @updatedAt injection and touches calendars outside the refreshed set
raw_findings.trigger: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache is invoked with a subset of a credential's calendars (e.g., the remainingCalendars path in unwatchCalendar), or a maintainer reads the empty {} data argument.

raw_findings.root_cause: BSD/macOS-specific sed -i '' syntax used in a cross-platform developer script.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a portable in-place edit, e.g. write to a temp file and mv it, or detect the platform (sed -i vs sed -i '').

finding.verifier_reason: CalendarsRouterHandlerCache is a type hint for lazy-loaded handlers, not a strict contract. The deleteCache route works correctly without being in this cache type. This is a minor style/documentation inconsistency, not a functional defect.

rejected_findings.reason: CalendarsRouterHandlerCache is a type hint for lazy-loaded handlers, not a strict contract. The deleteCache route works correctly without being in this cache type. This is a minor style/documentation inconsistency, not a functional defect.

finding.body: GNU sed treats '' as the backup-suffix argument's filename operand, erroring (e.g., "sed: can't read : No such file or directory") so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated and the tunnel URL is silently wrong for webhook testing.
finding.failure_mode: Script errors on Linux and leaves the stale GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in the env file.
finding.impact: GNU sed treats '' as the backup-suffix argument's filename operand, erroring (e.g., "sed: can't read : No such file or directory") so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated and the tunnel URL is silently wrong for webhook testing.
finding.root_cause: BSD/macOS-specific sed -i '' syntax used in a cross-platform developer script.
finding.suggested_fix: Use a portable in-place edit, e.g. write to a temp file and mv it, or detect the platform (sed -i vs sed -i '').
finding.title: sed -i '' in new webhook test script is macOS-only and fails on GNU sed
finding.trigger: A developer on Linux runs scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh when GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists in ../.env.
finding.verifier_reason: Line 68 shows 'sed -i '' -E' which is macOS BSD sed syntax. GNU sed on Linux interprets '' as a filename argument, causing the command to fail. This is a cross-platform compatibility bug in a developer script.

finding.evidence: export const deleteCacheHandler = async ({ ctx, input }: DeleteCacheOptions) => {
finding.failure_mode: Authorization behavior of the new destructive endpoint is unverified and unprotected against regression.
finding.impact: A security-relevant destructive mutation (deleting another user's calendar cache by credentialId) has no regression test, so an authorization regression would ship undetected.
finding.root_cause: New handler with an ownership-based authorization check was introduced without any accompanying test.
finding.suggested_fix: Add a unit test (mirroring existing handler tests / calendar-cache.repository.test.ts patterns) asserting that deleteCacheHandler rejects a credentialId owned by a different user and deletes rows only for an owned credential.
finding.title: No test coverage for deleteCacheHandler ownership check
finding.trigger: Future refactor of the credential lookup (e.g., dropping the userId filter or switching to findUnique on id) would remove the only authorization barrier for a destructive deleteMany.
finding.verifier_reason: Test coverage gaps are not defects introduced by the patch. The handler has authorization logic (userId filter at line 20). Absence of tests is a process concern, not a code defect with observable impact.

rejected_findings.reason: Test coverage gaps are not defects introduced by the patch. The handler has authorization logic (userId filter at line 20). Absence of tests is a process concern, not a code defect with observable impact.

validated_findings.body: The handler always executes a real prisma.calendarCache.groupBy query and surfaces cacheUpdatedAt in the UI even when the calendar-cache feature is globally disabled, contradicting the established gating pattern (CalendarCache.init returns the mock when disabled) and adding an unconditional DB query per request.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Cache status UI and DB queries occur even when calendar caching is disabled, showing stale/irrelevant cache data and diverging from the mock/flag contract.
validated_findings.impact: The handler always executes a real prisma.calendarCache.groupBy query and surfaces cacheUpdatedAt in the UI even when the calendar-cache feature is globally disabled, contradicting the established gating pattern (CalendarCache.init returns the mock when disabled) and adding an unconditional DB query per request.
validated_findings.root_cause: Direct construction of CalendarCacheRepository instead of using the feature-flag-aware CalendarCache.init factory that the codebase uses everywhere else.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Obtain the repository via CalendarCache.init(null) (or an equivalent flag-aware factory) so the mock is used and no cache status is shown when the feature is disabled.
validated_findings.title: connectedCalendars handler bypasses calendar-cache feature flag by instantiating CalendarCacheRepository directly
validated_findings.trigger: Any user loads connected calendars while the global "calendar-cache" feature flag is disabled (the case CalendarCacheRepositoryMock exists for).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that CalendarCache.init is the 'established gating pattern' is incorrect. CalendarCacheRepository is a valid class that implements ICalendarCacheRepository. The handler directly queries cache status which is a separate concern from the CalendarCache.init factory used for caching availability. The repository context shows CalendarCacheRepository is a legitimate implementation, not a bypass.

validated_findings.body: tRPC surfaces the plain Error as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) instead of a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code, so clients cannot distinguish an authorization failure from a server fault and monitoring records spurious 500s.
validated_findings.evidence: throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied");
validated_findings.failure_mode: Authorization failures are misreported as internal server errors to clients and observability tooling.
validated_findings.impact: tRPC surfaces the plain Error as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) instead of a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code, so clients cannot distinguish an authorization failure from a server fault and monitoring records spurious 500s.
validated_findings.root_cause: New handler uses a generic Error where the tRPC layer expects TRPCError codes to communicate client-side failure semantics.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" }) (or "FORBIDDEN") as other viewer handlers do for missing/unowned resources.
validated_findings.title: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError for authorization failure
validated_findings.trigger: A user calls viewer.calendars.deleteCache with a credentialId they do not own (or a nonexistent/team-owned credential where userId is null).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 25 shows 'throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")' which is a plain Error. In tRPC, plain Errors become INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than semantic codes like NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN. Other handlers in the codebase use TRPCError for authorization failures. This is a valid API design issue.

validated_findings.body: The cache_last_updated timestamp is always rendered in US date/time format (MM/DD/YY, 12-hour clock) regardless of the user's locale, producing inconsistent and potentially confusing localized UI.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Non-English users see US-formatted timestamps embedded in otherwise translated text.
validated_findings.impact: The cache_last_updated timestamp is always rendered in US date/time format (MM/DD/YY, 12-hour clock) regardless of the user's locale, producing inconsistent and potentially confusing localized UI.
validated_findings.root_cause: Locale string hardcoded in the new Intl.DateTimeFormat call while the surrounding component is fully localized.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the user's locale (e.g., from useLocale's i18n.language) to Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of hardcoding "en-US".
validated_findings.title: Cache timestamp is hardcoded to en-US locale ignoring the user's locale
validated_findings.trigger: A user with a non-English locale (the component already calls useLocale for translations) opens the credential dropdown showing cache status.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 89 shows 'new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US"' hardcoded while the component uses useLocale() for translations. The timestamp will display in US format regardless of user locale, creating inconsistent localization.

validated_findings.body: The UI shows an active 'Cache Status / Last updated' entry and a delete option for cache data that is already expired and unusable, misrepresenting cache freshness to the user.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Stale/expired cache rows are presented as live cache status in the settings UI.
validated_findings.impact: The UI shows an active 'Cache Status / Last updated' entry and a delete option for cache data that is already expired and unusable, misrepresenting cache freshness to the user.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new groupBy query omits the expiresAt filter that every other read path in this repository applies.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } to the where clause (matching getCachedAvailability's filter) or expose expiry so the UI can distinguish expired caches.
validated_findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds reports status for expired cache rows
validated_findings.trigger: A credential has only CalendarCache rows whose expiresAt is in the past (cache no longer served by getCachedAvailability, which filters expiresAt >= now).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 174-182 show getCacheStatusByCredentialIds queries without expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability at line 127 filters 'expiresAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now()) }'. This means expired cache rows are included in status but not served, misrepresenting cache freshness.

validated_findings.body: SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is bumped for every calendar under the credential — including calendars whose cache was not refreshed in this call — and the update only works because Prisma implicitly injects @updatedAt into an empty data object, an obscure side effect that is easy to break during refactoring.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Freshness timestamps are set on rows that were not refreshed, and the intended timestamp bump silently disappears if the implicit @updatedAt behavior changes.
validated_findings.impact: SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is bumped for every calendar under the credential — including calendars whose cache was not refreshed in this call — and the update only works because Prisma implicitly injects @updatedAt into an empty data object, an obscure side effect that is easy to break during refactoring.
validated_findings.root_cause: New updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty update object and a credential-wide predicate instead of an explicit field update scoped to the refreshed calendars.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass an explicit { updatedAt: new Date() } payload and scope the update to the selectedCalendars actually refreshed (e.g., by externalId/eventTypeId) rather than all rows for the credential.
validated_findings.title: Empty-data updateMany relies on implicit @updatedAt injection and touches calendars outside the refreshed set
validated_findings.trigger: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache is invoked with a subset of a credential's calendars (e.g., the remainingCalendars path in unwatchCalendar), or a maintainer reads the empty {} data argument.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 1024 shows 'updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})' with empty data object. The schema at line 860 shows 'updatedAt DateTime? @updatedAt' which Prisma auto-updates. However, this updates ALL calendars under the credential, not just those refreshed in the loop. The implicit behavior and over-broad scope are valid concerns.
